why: The consumers this package holds itself to, declared rather than remembered.
The roadmap named Shio and Turing throughout while dumont-react sat on the
same 2026.3 line consuming the same entries, so one-look claims were being
checked against two of three. This file is the one place that set lives:
prose that names a subset as though it were the whole is a test failure,
not a style note.
VDS73 widened it again, and by more than the line predicted. It expected two
Next installs; three consumers were absent, because cloud-frontend is a Vite
SPA nobody had written down either. Being outside the products root that
`use:local` walks is what kept all three invisible: the loop this package
offers instead of a publish could not reach them, so nothing ever asked.
`framework` is why the membership could not just grow. A Next consumer takes
a different set: no `./router`, because the App Router is what replaces
react-router-dom, and no `./vite`. A guard that assumes every consumer
resolves `./router` asserts something three of six cannot do.
`chrome` says which surface, and `console` stopped covering it: a platform
home and a public admissions front door are neither consoles nor bento.
VDS144 made it a measurement. `pnpm chrome:census` counts the source files that
take a console-era component, from the package or through a product's own
re-export shim, and holds the field to that count: `console` for a consumer
that takes one and not ./bento, `mixed` for one that takes both, and anything
else only at zero. The first reading moved three: Turing had been called
`bento` with sixteen files still on console-era headers and empty states,
Dumont `console` while taking ./bento too, and the Cloud Console `console` with
no console-era import at all. The non-goals that wait for every console to cut
over are waiting for no entry to say `console` or `mixed`.
VDS147 is that reading arriving. Turing and Dumont finished their cutover, the
census counted zero console-era imports in all nine, and both entries moved from
`mixed` to `bento` — which is what allowed the eleven console-era components to
be removed. The field stays measured rather than retired: it is how the next
chrome, whatever it is, gets counted instead of remembered.
VDS146 took `console` and `mixed` out of the vocabulary. They named a chrome a
consumer could still be rendering, and there is no longer one to render: the
components are gone and so is the provider that picked between them. So the
census stopped asking a consumer to agree with its own measurement and now
reports a counted console-era import on its own, which is the only thing left
that could put one there — a name coming back, in a product, where this
repository's own removal guard cannot see it.
`accent` is the token set a consumer renders with, and today every one of
them says `cool`. That is worth recording rather than assuming: VDS23 made
the brand accent a token so a product could re-key without forking a header,
and no product has re-keyed yet. The parity digest reads this, so the day one
does, the digest is required to carry that set.
VDS122 widened it a third time, to nine, and the two it added were invisible
for a third reason: both take the package by caret range rather than pinning
it, so each receives a release the moment it installs one, and neither is a
product — a marketing site and a docs site are not what a guard here goes
looking for. Both were reached by reading their imports, not by being
remembered. `viglet-docs` is also the first consumer on a third framework;
it takes no root entry at all, only `./preset` and the background.
`entries` is what each product imports, and VDS129 is why that is measured
rather than copied in. A snapshot drifted exactly as it was expected to: the
Shio entry listed three of the six subpaths its source takes and still said
`console`, and five other entries had gained or lost a subpath too, while the
only guard asked whether a declared entry exists and never whether an
imported one is declared.
`sourceRoots` says where a product's own source is, relative to its package
root, so the measure is declared rather than guessed. `viglet-ds-consumer-entries`
reads them from a consumer's checkout and fails in both directions: a subpath
imported and not declared, and one declared and imported nowhere. Tests and
stories inside those roots are skipped, since a census test that greps for a
subpath is counting pages, not taking the entry. This file ships in the package
so a consumer can run that from its own suite.
`checkout` is where `use:local` finds a consumer, relative to this repository's
root, with `{line}` standing for the version line this checkout is cut from.
The loop used to walk the directory above this checkout, which stopped being a
products root once this repository moved to one worktree per version, and it
found nothing (VDS130). A consumer not checked out beside this one says
`offMachine: true` instead, so on a developer's machine a checkout that is not
there is a failing test rather than a sentence nobody reads.
